filename: An Unsupervised Learning Perspective on the Dynamic Contribution to Extreme Precipitation Changes.pdf
title: An Unsupervised Learning Perspective on the Dynamic Contribution to Extreme Precipitation Changes
venue: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop at NeurIPS 2022
testbed_rationale: Although high-resolution superparameterized (SPCAM) data was simulated, no direct data or code repository URL is provided to make it an off-the-shelf testbed candidate.
pain_points: Simulations output massive multi-scale, three-dimensional data (3.4 TB, >76 million snapshots) that challenge standard analysis tools.
Lack of samples at the very high tails of the precipitation distribution (>99th percentile) causing noisy/pixelated spatial patterns.
Difficulty in isolating dynamical contributions from thermodynamic contributions without sacrificing storm-scale spatial information.
extraction_notes: The paper focuses on using an unsupervised VAE and K-means clustering to decompose dynamic versus thermodynamic components of extreme precipitation changes under uniform +4K SST warming in SPCAM. Note mentions of DYAMOND data management via DKRZ appear in acknowledgments, but the primary dataset analyzed is from SPCAM simulations performed by the authors.
